/-!
# Erdős Problem 246

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/246](https://www.erdosproblems.com/246)
- [Bi59] Birch, B. J., *Note on a problem of Erd\H{o}s*. Proc. Cambridge
  Philos. Soc. (1959), 370-373.
- [Ca60] Cassels, J. W. S., *On the representation of integers as the sums of
  distinct summands taken from a fixed set*. Acta Sci. Math. (Szeged) (1960),
  111-124.
- [FaCh17] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *A quantitative form of the
  {E}rd\H{o}s-{B}irch theorem*. Acta Arith. (2017), 301--311.
- [He00b] Hegyv\'{a}ri, N., *On the completeness of an exponential type
  sequence*. Acta Math. Hungar. (2000), 127--135.
- [Yu24] Yu, Wang-Xing, *On the representation of an exponential type sequence*.
  Publ. Math. Debrecen (2024), 253--261.
-/

namespace Erdos246

/-- The set $\{a^k b^l : k,l \geq 0\}$. -/
def Gamma (a b : ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  {x | ∃ k l : ℕ, x = a ^ k * b ^ l}

/--
Let $(a,b)=1$. The set $\{a^kb^l: k,l\geq 0\}$ is complete - that is, every large integer is the sum of distinct integers of the form $a^kb^l$ with $k,l\geq 0$.

We state the nontrivial case $a,b\geq 2$, proved by Birch [Bi59].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos246.lean"]
theorem erdos_246 (a b : ℕ) (ha : 2 ≤ a) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) :
    IsAddComplete (Gamma a b) := by
  sorry

end Erdos246

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement uses completeness of a set of integer values, whereas Birch’s theorem as restated in Fang–Chen, Theorem A, explicitly represents sufficiently large integers using distinct nonnegative exponent pairs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For coprime a,b ≥ 2, the map (k,l) ↦ a^k*b^l is injective: equality of two products and coprimality give mutual divisibility of the powers of a, hence equality of their exponents; cancellation then gives equality of the exponents of b. Finite images and preimages therefore preserve distinctness and sums. Unfolding IsAddComplete gives exactly an existential threshold followed by such a representation for every n above it. This biconditional was proved in /workspace/review/pair-equivalence.lean, with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound as axioms. The equivalent finite-complement formulation used by the external proof was also checked in Lean.

review.notes: Both Gamma and erdos_246 faithfully state the cited mathematics. The assumptions a,b ≥ 2 are explicit in Fang–Chen’s Theorem A and Yu’s abstract, although the problem website leaves them implicit. Lean tests checked zero exponents, excluded bases 0 and 1, empty sums, satisfiable hypotheses at (2,3), non-completeness of Gamma 1 1, and sample subset sums. The website records PROVED (LEAN), agreeing with the file’s metadata. The external proof has matching hypotheses and an equivalent conclusion, with no explicit sorry or custom axiom declarations found; its original Lean 4.29.1 build was not independently reproduced because only 4.33.1 is available and compilation encountered compatibility errors. This is not evidence of a mathematical or status defect. Scratch checks compiled successfully, and the reviewed file was not modified.
